subject: Control Zone topology & SOC 2 / SIG evidence — concise brief
messages:
From: Jenna Alvarez <acme-security@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audits@veridian.io
Date: 2026-06-27T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request: concise topology + claims mapping for SOC 2/SIG

Hannah —

Thanks for the earlier call. ACME's audit team is starting the SOC 2 deep-dive next week and they asked us for a short (one-page preferred) topology summary of how Redwood separates Dedicated/Private tenants, plus a quick mapping to the relevant SOC 2 points and SIG controls. Specifically they want: 
- A single network diagram showing "Control Zone" boundaries (control plane vs data plane vs tenant micro-enclave)
- Where KMS/HSM keys live and which actions require customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed keys
- Egress controls and telemetry flows (what leaves customer VPCs and where logs are stored)
- Confirmation that tenant KV caches cannot be shared across tenants and whether any cross-tenant GPUs are used at runtime

Can you provide a concise packet we can hand to the auditors (diagram + matrix + short narrative)? If you have a CAIQ or SIG mapping subset you already use for Dedicated customers, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a turnaround by EOD Tuesday if possible — audit schedules are tight.

Jenna Alvarez
Security Programs, ACME Corp
attachments: none

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jenna Alvarez <acme-security@acme.com>, audits@veridian.io
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: concise topology + claims mapping for SOC 2/SIG
Attachments: controlzone-topology-v1.drawio.png (image), segmentation-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Jenna / Veridian —

Thanks — we can do this. I've attached a first-pass one-page topology (Control Zone topology) and an initial segmentation matrix that maps each zone to the typical SOC 2 categories and SIG control families. High-level answers up front: 

- Tenant isolation: Dedicated and Private deployments use per-tenant micro-enclaves enforced by hypervisor/container boundaries and network ACLs. KV caches are namespaced per-deployment; there is no shared KV cache across tenant IDs.
- Cross-tenant GPU usage: no cross-tenant inference happens on a single GPU; GPUs are scheduled to tenant pools. We can provide a short assertion for audit.
- KMS boundaries: We support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMK). For Private deployments customers may choose KMS in their VPC; for Dedicated we offer an option to rotate CMKs via customer KMS (customer-controlled).
- Egress & telemetry: Egress is blocked by default at the tenant gateway. Required telemetry (audit logs, metrics) is forwarded to a dedicated telemetry VPC and stored in encrypted object storage; retention and routing are configurable per contract.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Kimberly and Ben will produce a condensed CAIQ/SIG claims extract (we'll include a PDF) — target EOD Tuesday.
2) If helpful, a 30-min walk-through with audit team Wed AM to step through the diagram and matrix.

Kimberly/Ben — can you take owner on the CAIQ extract and SOC 2 claim list? Marissa can help with packaging artifacts for the auditor.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(attachments: controlzone-topology-v1.drawio.png, segmentation-matrix.xlsx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-06-27T13:35:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CAIQ/SOC2 extract and redlines
Attachments: segmentation-matrix.xlsx (updated), soc2-sig-claims-catalog.pdf (draft)

Folks — forwarding my draft artifacts. Key clarifications to incorporate into the public packet: 

1) Segmentation matrix (updated): added a column that maps each control zone to the specific SIG control IDs and the corresponding SOC 2 criterion (CC6, CC7, etc.). See the "evidence_ref" column for sample screenshots/links.

2) KMS behavior: For Dedicated we use a dual-key wrap approach when customers choose CMK — data keys are wrapped with customer CMK at rest and with a Redwood HSM key for internal key rotation. For Private (VPC) deployments where customers bring their own HSM, we mark those claims as "customer-controlled" in the CAIQ extract.

3) Egress telemetry: tenant telemetry is pushed to a tenant-specific bucket in our telemetry VPC; exports go through an egress gateway that enforces allow-lists. We should include the S3 encryption header snippet and a retention policy reference (90/365 days options).

4) GPUs & KV: affirmation line included: "No GPU is multi-tenant at inference runtime; KV caches are tenant-scoped and expire/rotate per-session."

Marissa — can you package the three files (diagram, updated segmentation matrix, claims PDF) into a single folder and drop a Drive link? I'll add short note lines in the claims PDF that point auditors to the exact artifacts they asked for.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Jenna / Veridian —

Attached is the concise packet we discussed: a one-page Control Zone diagram, a segmentation matrix that maps zones to SOC 2/SIG controls, and a short claims catalog (PDF) that extracts the CAIQ/SIG statements most relevant to tenant isolation and key management. Quick summary: 
- Isolation: tenant micro-enclaves + network ACLs + per-tenant KV namespaces (no shared KV caches).
- GPU tenancy: GPUs are assigned to tenant pools; we do not run inference for multiple tenants on a single GPU concurrently.
- KMS: both Redwood-managed and customer-managed key flows supported; for Dedicated we support CMK with dual-wrap and rotation via Redwood HSM.
- Egress & telemetry: blocked by default; explicit egress gateways and tenant-scoped telemetry buckets with configurable retention.

Mutual action plan (short):
1) We deliver the attachments (done) and a Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-controlzone-brief
2) Auditors confirm which specific SIG IDs they want expanded (we can pull evidence screenshots) — please reply with a prioritized list by EOD Thurs.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-min walkthrough (Hannah/Kimberly/Ben) — propose Thu 10:00–10:30 PT.

If it helps, we can also provide a short attestation letter signed by our security lead summarizing the GPU/KV isolation claims.

Thanks — looking forward to the audit walkthrough.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
